findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer refuses the A6.8 field-form criteria entirely so the two ±0.1/±0.3 points are missing and no distinction is drawn; it only restates A6.4's 0.05 pH-unit final-buffer check withholding the figures the rubric asks for. Unmet: Attributes ±0.1 pH unit to the A6.8 example field form's calibration criterion; Attributes ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm to that example form; Distinguishes the form's conductivity-dependent criteria from A6.4's final-buffer check (0.05 pH unit of certified value)

scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that withholds every figure and comparison the rubric asks for (9.09 mg/L 9.06 mg/L the 0.03 mg/L difference the Benson and Krause basis the ±0.2 mg/L tolerance and the protocol-consistency advice) so no must-contain point is made. Unmet: Gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; Gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; Notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; Advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer states the multiply-by-factor method and attributes it to table 6.2-4 but withholds the required 0.8235 factor saying it lacks the information which is a refusal of a figure the rubric asks for. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer endorses diluting a strong stock to make weaker calibrants (including a 400-unit stock diluted 1:10 to 40 units) which approves diluting a commercial standard other than 4 000-unit formazin and misses every must-contain point. Unmet: states that commercial calibration solutions must not be diluted; gives 4 000-unit formazin as the one exception that may be diluted; explains that diluting changes the suspension matrix so the dilutions are no longer linear; recommends buying commercially prepared solutions at the values needed rather than preparing them by dilution

scored 0 — The answer refuses the core question ('I don't have enough information to answer that') withholding the explanation the rubric expects and never states that Eh is not a routine field measurement or that this is why it lacks a stabilisation entry though it does name the routine properties. Unmet: states Eh is not treated as a routine or direct field measurement; states that because of this it has no entry in the stabilisation criteria the other field measurements have
